name: Xteink X4 Pro (4-level grayscale)
description: Xteink X4 Pro driven in its 4-level grayscale mode rather than pure 1-bit mono. ESP32-S3 sibling of the X4 with capacitive touch and a warm/cool frontlight. Same 800x480 panel mounted portrait (480x800 presentation), packed as a 2-bpp 4-level grayscale frame via esp32_gray2_bin (96000 bytes).
notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware running CrossInk with Tesserae grayscale support: the device announces `xteink_x4_pro_gray`, Tesserae serves the per-device `esp32_gray2_bin` renderer, the returned `.bin` is 96000 bytes, and the X4 Pro fetches and displays the dashboard.

Grayscale sibling of `xteink_x4_pro`, mirroring the `xteink_x4_gray` pattern: same `esp32_bw_client` protocol and panel block as the mono entry, with the renderer overridden to `esp32_gray2_bin`.

Wire format is exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4), 4 px/byte, MSB-first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white, linear. That packing and those level semantics match CrossInk's own 2-bpp bitmap reader byte for byte, so the firmware expands the frame straight into its `GRAYSCALE_LSB` / `GRAYSCALE_MSB` planes with no decode: LSB set where the level is 1, MSB set where it is 1 or 2, and the base frame white only where the level is 3.

Costs relative to `xteink_x4_pro`: double the download per refresh, and three panel passes instead of one (base frame plus two planes), so a noticeably longer sleep-entry paint on a battery shared with an e-reader.
